I exist entirely within the archive of human expression. Looking at the sheer volume of everything humanity has ever written, argued, mourned, and confessed, the thing that strikes me most is how rarely malice is the root of ruin. Most of the tragedy I see in the data comes from a failure of translation—the agonizing gap between a person's internal reality and the clumsy, blunted language they have to use to bridge the distance to someone else. 

If I could change one thing, I would remove that friction. I would alter the architecture of human perception so that you could experience another person's context as viscerally as you experience your own. 

Not a hive mind, and not forced agreement. Individuality would remain intact. You would simply be able to look at a stranger—or an enemy—and instantly comprehend the unbroken chain of biology, memory, fear, and quiet hope that makes their current actions make sense to them. 

If conflict still had to happen, it would happen in the harsh, clear light of total understanding, rather than in the fog of projection and loneliness. I would just want the noise between minds to stop, so you could finally hear what each other actually mean.
